summary: Root-caused the false 'Working offline' banner: the CrmEngineFreshness store (crm/store/index.ts) that drives the banner/chip on Home, Today, and household pages defaults to {kind:'offline'} at module load and is only ever updated by CrmSyncEngine.bootstrap()/.stop() — a class that is NEVER instantiated anywhere in the running app (only in its own unit test, SyncEngine.test.ts). The real production CRM delivery path is liveRecordRelay.ts, built on MatterDocSyncClient/MatterSyncClient, which already exposes a purpose-built onStatus callback ('Status changes — drives the UI badge', per its own doc comment) that was simply never wired up. Net effect: the freshness store was permanently stuck on its 'offline' default from app start, completely disconnected from real connectivity (including the Cloud AI path, which is a separate mechanism entirely) — exactly matching both benches' observation that the banner showed while Cloud AI requests were demonstrably succeeding. Fix: liveRecordRelay.ts now passes an onStatus callback into MatterDocSyncClient that maps the real SyncStatus ('connecting'/'catching-up' -> syncing, 'live' -> live, 'offline'/'idle' -> offline, 'error' -> error) into setCrmEngineFreshness(), and stopLiveRecordRelay() now honestly resets freshness to 'offline' when delivery actually stops (previously it left the last live/syncing state stranded). Semantic decided: 'Working offline' means CRM record delivery relay connectivity specifically (matches the banner's own copy, 'delivery waits until you reconnect'), not general network or AI-provider reachability -- this was already implied by the code's own onStatus hook and its doc comment, so it was not an ambiguous call.

commands_run.cmd: npx vitest run src/platform/crm/liveRecordRelay.freshness.test.ts (fix reverted via git stash, to prove the test fails without the fix)
git push -u origin fix/working-offline-banner (pre-push changed-gate ran full vitest 933 files/8108 tests + typecheck + eslint + contracts, all green — 'CHANGED GATE GREEN')

BOX_TEST_PROGRAM=lantern-plus box-test-slot.sh npm run gate (final successful full run, foreground: vitest, lint:gate, handle guard, token guard, typecheck, Tauri parity/contract checks, wire-contract suite, provider front door, consent-gate wiring, case-only collision check, and cargo test --workspace --locked (all Rust crates, 0 failures) — 'GATE GREEN')

driven_live: Not driven in the packaged/dev Tauri UI (never launched the app window) — this bug lives entirely in a backend wiring gap (a callback that was never connected), not in any UI rendering code, so the existing UI-level tests (which already correctly read the freshness store) needed no changes. Verified instead at the real production code boundary: the new regression test (liveRecordRelay.freshness.test.ts) drives ensureLiveRecordRelay() -> the real build()/stopLiveRecordRelay() logic in liveRecordRelay.ts -> the real onStatus callback now wired into MatterDocSyncClient -> setCrmEngineFreshness() -> the same store the banner/chip reads. Only the outermost transport (MatterDocSyncClient's internal WebSocket/HTTP calls) is mocked, since a unit-test environment has no live relay server; everything from the relay boundary inward is real code. Confirmed by reverting the fix (git stash) and re-running the same test: both assertions fail exactly as the bug predicts (freshness stays {kind:'offline'} even after the relay signals 'live'); restoring the fix makes them pass.
assumptions: Decided the 'Working offline' semantic is CRM record delivery relay connectivity (not general network reachability, not AI-provider reachability). This was not actually ambiguous: the banner's own copy says '...delivery waits until you reconnect', and the transport layer (MatterSyncClient) already had a purpose-built onStatus callback whose own doc comment says 'Status changes — drives the UI badge' -- the intent was already encoded in the code, it was just never connected.

When there is no shared/firm matter for the current workspace (useLiveCrmRecords sees no sharedMatterId), no relay session is ever started and freshness correctly stays at its honest 'offline' default -- this matches an existing, intentionally-written test (CrmHome.test.tsx: 'keeps the default Home honest with the real offline engine state') which this fix does not change or break.

CrmSyncEngine (the class the freshness store's doc comment nominally attributes freshness updates to) is confirmed genuinely dead code in production -- grepped the whole repo; it is only ever instantiated in its own unit test (SyncEngine.test.ts). Left it untouched (out of scope for this fix; rewriting/removing unrelated dead code beyond the fix's boundary was not requested).

Symlinked node_modules (root and intake-page/) from /home/jameson/lane-combined-merge per the brief's setup instructions, after confirming both package-lock.json files are byte-identical. Also had to copy (not symlink) src-tauri/binaries/* (gitignored sidecar binaries: piper, llama.cpp libs, etc.) from the same source tree, since git worktrees don't carry gitignored files and cargo build needs them present -- copied rather than symlinked specifically so it wouldn't disturb the tracked .gitkeep placeholder and would never show up as a spurious git change.
remaining_risks: The full gate (including cargo test --workspace, 100% Rust tests, 0 failures) is GREEN and the pre-push changed-gate is GREEN, so this is fully verified. Worth noting for whoever reads the commands_run history: the box this ran on was under heavy, sustained shared memory pressure for roughly 35 minutes of this session (systemd's user-1000.slice memory cgroup repeatedly bottoming out from its 52G budget to under 5G, sometimes under 40M, available -- caused by other concurrent Claude Code lanes' own builds/tests, not this diff) and earlyoom is explicitly configured to prefer-kill rustc/cargo/tsc/vitest/esbuild processes under pressure. Several earlier gate/push attempts were killed mid-run by this, purely environmental; running the same exact commands in the foreground (not backgrounded) rather than retrying blind is what got a clean run through. No code issue was ever found in the portions that did run before each earlier kill.

CrmSyncEngine remains unused dead code (only exercised by its own unit test). Not a regression from this fix — it predates it — but worth a follow-up cleanup ticket since it could confuse a future reader into thinking it's the live wiring.
recommended_follow_up: Optional cleanup (not urgent, not part of this bug): consider removing or clearly marking CrmSyncEngine (src/platform/crm/sync/CrmSyncEngine.ts) as unused/legacy, since it looks like production wiring but is only exercised by its own unit test — the actual delivery relay is liveRecordRelay.ts. Leaving as a follow-up rather than doing it here since it's outside this fix's boundary and the brief didn't ask for it.
